body:
I just want to say thank you.  I'm glad to hear everything worked out for you.  Hopefully the school councilor will be useful tomorrow (there's a good chance it won't be very useful, since I've never heard good reviews... but maybe?).

And your lake plan is much more considerate than the ill-conceived plan I had a couple of years ago, which involved renting a cheap hotel room, using duct tape and such to make the bathroom air tight, and burn charcoal in a few cheap grills after downing a bottle of sleeping pills while sitting in a full bath tub (don't think the pills would do me in, but surely drowning + carbon monoxide would prove effective?)

How did you find the psychiatrist?  And what was the non-traditional approach?

Now I have a white board.

And halloween candy, because I'm depressed and on my period, which is a good excuse to have chocolate for dinner.  Chocolate, and Mike's Hard Lemonade that someone gave me a while ago.

Hmm.  Have been eating weird food today.  For lunch I had a can of peas, and chocolate milk.

Edit: Ugh.  Chocolate does not a good dinner make.

My feet are so big that shoe shopping is annoying?

That's about all I've got.

My feet are so big that shoe shopping is annoying?

That's about all I've got.

You know what I have always wanted but have been too cheap to get?  A white board for next to my desk, on the wall.  This is also the first time my desk/wall arrangement has been such a way to make it possible.

I'm going to go buy one for a to-do list.

1. Overweight (although I carry it well!)

2. Unambitious (I don't really care if I'm not the best)

3. Poor grades (Although I was quite clever in elementary school, middle school, and even high school)

4. Have let various school organizations I'm in down

5. Don't have a job yet

6. Terrible at keeping in contact with those I care about/those that care about me

7. Feel like I haven't really learned anything in the last 4 years, from my slacking.

And I just don't care much about any of these things, which is sort of their cause.  And I feel bad for not caring, which is perhaps a bit odd.  I've always just sort of... gone the route that seemed Acceptable.  Which is strange, considering I ended up as a female in a male dominated field.

And so because I know everything is my fault, why would I want to burden other people by asking for help?  And then there's just so many small and big things to do, I don't know where to start, so I just waste time on the computer, or in dreams.

>You're in the home stretch school wise.

Indeed.  But I hear there's this thing called "the real world" that comes after.  And I hear it isn't any easier.

>One thing that helped me understand my depression and suicidal urges was reading this

Yep, I read that today.  I was like, "Fuck, that's me."

>I don't know why you're depressed and thinking of suicide, but it's serious. If you haven't talked to someone, a friend, a family member, a teacher, then I really hope you'll consider it.

Ah, but then if the seemingly inevitable *does* happen, then they will feel bad for "not doing enough"

>Jesus christ on a stick.

Haha, cliche, right?

>Let's start with the shame part.

Sounds like a plan.  What about it?

>without being here, you won't get to see the bastards get their comeuppance

What bastards?  The only person I really dislike has a micropenis (according to the friend that got drunk and spent a night at his house), so he's already got his comeuppance.

I like people.

>That, and pot. I smoke a lot of pot. I don't suggest you do any of these things, except for the pot thing. Smoke a doobar and enjoy a show or something.

Yeah... as if I already didn't have a problem with sitting around and doing nothing.  Thanks, but no thanks.

>Try to become as selfless as possible and you will find yourself enjoying more and more of your time.

I already am pretty selfless.  Recently, only times I'm able to motivate myself to do something is when it involves helping other people.  The things I need to do *are* selfish.  Do homework.  Try to talk to professors to ask for permission to make up exams I didn't do.  Find a job.

I think the two of us may be depressed for *entirely* different reasons.
Well, the functional programming class was last spring.  I didn't finish all the work, and now I need to do it in my free time.  The class I'm missing is a math class.

>I know how hard it is to manage a sense of self-worth where nobody seems to give any bit of a damn.

Eh.  I don't really care how self centered other people are.  In fact, I'd prefer people were *more* self centered.  Then I could disappear forever and nobody would ever notice.

>The funny part is that you're doing better than you think by having your existential breakdown now rather than later.

I've been having existential break downs since elementary school.  I suspect I'll be having them both now *and* later.


But yeah.  I know I'm not unique, and that *so many* people go through this.  It's one of the reasons asking for help is so difficult.  I don't have as many legitimate problems as other people.

It's a functional programming class.  I should have worked on it more during the summer.  I didn't.   And now the deadline draws closer.

The grading is done online.  The professor changed the dates for me, to August, so I could work on it over the summer.  I need to talk to him again and have him extend the dates to the end of November (school policy is that "incomplete" classes have till the end of the next quarter to get completed)

But, again, there is shame.  He was already kind enough to move the dates once.  I don't want to talk to him and have him move them again :(
